reads.heading: What beekeeper reads
reads.body: beekeeper reads the session files Claude Code writes under ~/.claude/projects and shows what each agent did, changed, and cost. It only reads. It never writes to ~/.claude or to your repositories.

local.heading: Nothing leaves your computer
local.body: beekeeper makes no network requests and sends no telemetry. Everything you see is worked out locally from those files.

macos.heading: Why macOS may ask for folder access
macos.body: To show what an agent changed, beekeeper runs read-only git commands in the repository a session worked in. When that is a worktree under a protected folder such as Documents, Desktop, or Downloads, macOS asks whether beekeeper may access it. Allow it to see that worktree's changes. If you decline, beekeeper hides those changes and everything else keeps working.
